concepts.name: Garba and Dandiya Raas: Distinction, Origin, and Occasion
key_dimensions: Garba as a pre-worship dance performed BEFORE the idol vs. Dandiya Raas performed AFTER aarti — a common UPSC trap
Garba's association with Goddess Shakti/Navratri vs. Dandiya's association with Durga-Mahishasura legend
Instruments and props: Garba uses clapping/body percussion; Dandiya uses decorated sticks
Geographic spread: Gujarat origin vs. its adaptation in Rajasthan and overlap confusion in exams

concepts.name: Bihu Dance: Three Forms and Their Cultural Significance
key_dimensions: Three types — Rongali (Bohag/spring), Kongali (Kati/autumn), Bhogali (Magh/harvest) and their seasonal/agricultural linkages
Rongali Bihu as the only form with elaborate dance tradition vs. other two being more ritualistic
Instruments: Dhol, Pepa (buffalo horn), Gogona (jaw harp) — instrument-to-dance association
Bihu as a state festival of Assam cutting across caste and community lines — secular folk tradition angle

concepts.name: Chhau Dance: Three Regional Variants and Their Differences
key_dimensions: Three variants: Seraikella (Jharkhand), Purulia (West Bengal), Mayurbhanj (Odisha) — Mayurbhanj is the ONLY one performed WITHOUT masks
UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage status (inscribed 2010) — often asked
Themes: Martial arts, mythology (Mahabharata/Ramayana), nature — overlap with classical dance themes
Seraikella Chhau's royal patronage origin vs. Purulia Chhau's tribal/folk grassroots origin

concepts.name: Kalbelia Dance: Community Identity and GI/UNESCO Recognition
key_dimensions: Performed exclusively by the Kalbelia (snake charmer) community of Rajasthan — community-specific dance
UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage inscription in 2010 — same year as Chhau, a common confusion point
Costume and movement: Black swirling skirts mimicking serpent movement — symbolism angle
Gulabo Sapera as a prominent exponent — personality-to-art linkage questions

concepts.name: Lavani: Social Commentary and Regional Variants
key_dimensions: Maharashtra's Lavani: Two types — Nirguni (philosophical/spiritual) and Shringari (erotic/romantic) — often only Shringari is remembered
Dholki as the primary instrument — instrument identification trap
Historical role in boosting morale of Maratha soldiers — historical context angle
Tamasha theatre connection: Lavani as the core performative element of Tamasha folk theatre

concepts.name: Ghoomar: Rajasthani Folk Dance vs. Its Tribal Associations
key_dimensions: Originally a dance of the Bhil tribe later adopted by Rajput women — tribal-to-mainstream transition
Performed during auspicious occasions — bride's welcome into new home (a specific ritual context)
Confusion with Gair dance of Rajasthan (performed by men during Holi) — overlapping Rajasthani dances trap
Circular swirling movement with ghagra as defining visual element — art form identification

concepts.name: Yakshagana: Interface Between Folk and Classical Traditions
key_dimensions: Karnataka's Yakshagana: combination of dance, music, dialogue, costume — NOT purely a dance form
Two main styles: Tenkutittu (southern style) and Badagutittu (northern style) — regional sub-variants
Themes exclusively from Hindu epics/Puranas — thematic constraint unlike some secular folk dances
Distinction from Kerala's Krishnanattam and Kathakali — overlap with neighboring classical/semi-classical traditions

concepts.name: Theyyam: Ritual Dance of Kerala and Its Caste Dimensions
key_dimensions: Performed predominantly by lower-caste communities (Malayan, Vannan, Velan) — social inversion during performance
Performer becomes the deity — NOT mere enactment but divine possession concept
Confined to northern Kerala (Malabar region) — geographic specificity trap vs. pan-Kerala assumption
Distinction from Kathakali: Theyyam is ritualistic/outdoor/community-specific; Kathakali is classical/stage-based

concepts.name: Odissi-Adjacent Folk Dances of Odisha: Gotipua and Sambalpuri
key_dimensions: Gotipua: performed by young boys dressed as females — precursor tradition to classical Odissi dance
Sambalpuri folk dance linked to Sambalpuri weaving tradition — art form cluster concept
Dalkhai dance of western Odisha performed by women of tribal communities during festivals
Confusion trap: Odissi is classical; Gotipua/Sambalpuri are folk — frequently mixed in questions

concepts.name: Bhangra and Giddha: Gender-Specific Folk Dances of Punjab
key_dimensions: Bhangra: male harvest dance associated with Baisakhi; Giddha: female counterpart — gender specificity
Giddha incorporates 'Boliyan' (short witty poems) — unique literary element absent in Bhangra
Instruments: Dhol for Bhangra vs. Dholki for Giddha — instrument-gender-dance triangle
Contemporary globalization of Bhangra vs. Giddha remaining locally rooted — cultural diffusion angle

concepts.name: Manipuri Dance Traditions: Classical vs. Folk Overlap (Lai Haraoba)
key_dimensions: Lai Haraoba: pre-Vaishnavite Meitei folk ritual dance — predates classical Manipuri dance
Manipuri (classical) evolved FROM folk Lai Haraoba tradition — evolutionary linkage
Performed by Maibas and Maibis (priests and priestesses) — performer specificity
Trap: Manipuri in classical dance list (Sangeet Natak Akademi) vs. Lai Haraoba as folk — same region, different classification

concepts.name: Tribal Dances of Central India: Karma, Saila, and Panthi
key_dimensions: Karma dance: performed by Gond, Oraon, Baiga tribes during Karma festival worshipping the Karma tree — nature worship connection
Panthi dance: specific to Satnami community of Chhattisgarh — community-to-dance mapping
Saila: performed exclusively by boys during Kartik month — seasonal and gender specificity
Overlap trap: these dances span Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, MP — multi-state tribal dance traditions

concepts.name: Fugdi and Dekhni: Folk Dance Traditions of Goa
key_dimensions: Fugdi: performed by women in a circular formation without instruments — absence of instruments is a trap point
Dekhni: fusion of Indian and Portuguese elements — colonial cultural syncretism
Dhalo: another Goan women's dance performed only during winter (Pausha month) — seasonal restriction
Goa's folk dances reflecting Hindu-Christian-Portuguese syncretism — unique cultural layering

concepts.name: Nati and Kinnauri Nati: Mountain Folk Dance Traditions of Himachal Pradesh
key_dimensions: Nati recognized as the world's largest folk dance by Guinness World Records — record-based fact
Kinnauri Nati: specific to Kinnaur district, performed by both men and women holding each other's shoulders
Performed during festivals like Dussehra (Kullu Dussehra) — festival-dance linkage
Distinction from Jhora of Uttarakhand — neighboring hill state dance confusion

concepts.name: Kolattam and Karagattam: Tamil Nadu's Folk Dance Traditions
key_dimensions: Kolattam (stick dance): performed by women using sticks — similarity to Dandiya creates trap
Karagattam: balancing of decorated pots on head — prop-based identification; associated with Mariamman worship
Karagattam: two types — Aatta Karagam (joyful) and Sakthi Karagam (religious/solemn)
Therukoothu: Tamil street theatre with dance elements — overlap between folk dance and folk theatre

concepts.name: Santhali and Jharkhand Tribal Dances: Jhumair, Ho, and Mundari Traditions
key_dimensions: Jhumair: performed by Santhali and Kurukh communities — multi-tribe association
Domkach: performed during weddings by women of Jharkhand — occasion-specific identification
Ho tribe's dance traditions vs. Munda tribe — distinguishing tribal sub-group dances
Instruments: Madal drum as central instrument across Jharkhand tribal dances — unifying element

concepts.name: Dollu Kunitha and Veeragase: Karnataka's Ritual Folk Dances
key_dimensions: Dollu Kunitha: performed by Kuruba shepherd community — community specificity; Dollu is a large drum worn around neck
Veeragase: performed by devotees of Lord Shiva (Veerashaiva community) — religious-community linkage
Puja Kunitha: performed with decorated wooden structures (Kunitha) — prop identification
Distinction from Yakshagana: Kunitha dances are purely folk/devotional; Yakshagana is semi-theatrical

concepts.name: Folk Dances Associated with Harvest and Agricultural Cycles
key_dimensions: Harvest-linked dances: Bhangra (Punjab-Baisakhi), Bihu (Assam), Onam Thiruvathira (Kerala), Karma (tribal-central India) — cross-regional pattern
Sowing vs. harvest specificity — some dances mark sowing season, others post-harvest; exam often conflates them
Nature worship embedded in tribal agricultural dances — animism/totemism connection
Contrast: urban/royal folk dances (Ghoomar, Lavani with court patronage) vs. purely agrarian folk dances

concepts.name: Sangeet Natak Akademi and Zonal Cultural Centres: Institutional Support for Folk Dances
key_dimensions: Seven Zonal Cultural Centres (ZCCs) established in 1985 under Ministry of Culture — not under Sangeet Natak Akademi (common confusion)
Sangeet Natak Akademi awards for folk/tribal performing arts — institutional recognition mechanism
UNESCO ICH list vs. Sangeet Natak Akademi recognition — two different recognition frameworks
Tribes India initiative (TRIFED) — role in promoting tribal art including dance, distinct from culture ministry schemes

concepts.name: UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage: Indian Folk Dances on the List
key_dimensions: Chhau (2010) and Kalbelia (2010) inscribed in same year — high-frequency trap in prelims
Criteria for UNESCO ICH inscription vs. criteria for classical dance recognition by Sangeet Natak Akademi — different benchmarks
Ramlila, Vedic chanting, Ramman also on UNESCO list — distinguishing dance-specific entries from broader performing arts
What is NOT on UNESCO list despite being prominent: Bhangra, Garba — absence is equally important for exam
